# Plan and apply

How `callisto version` turns changesets into file edits, and where interrupted-command recovery stops. Behavior: [`docs/specs/versioning.json`](../specs/versioning.json). Write mechanics: [ADR 8](../adr/0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md). The emitted decision: [ADR 2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md).

## Two phases

| Phase | Entry point | Touches disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No |
| Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` |

- `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`).
- `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan.
- A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply.
- `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped.

## Idempotent apply

A crash can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same in-memory plan again is file-level idempotent; a fresh command does not retain that plan.

- Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`.
- A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`.
- Every consumed changeset path is staged whether or not the file still exists; deletions go through `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch`, so a file deleted before the crash is still removed from the index.
- `[workspace.package]` version writes (`VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage`) have no `from`/`to` precondition; they are written unconditionally.
- `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged.

## Command boundary and known gaps

`version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope.

`check_partial_run` refuses certain uncommitted bumps with E121: changed versions with changesets still present at HEAD, or staged canonical manifests outside pre mode. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply deletes consumed changesets before fallible lock refresh and staging; a failed refresh after consuming an untracked changeset can leave modified manifests, no decision and no detectable pending input. A fresh `version` is not guaranteed to recover that case.

The active-ecosystem collection currently chooses one ecosystem per bumped package. A dual Cargo/npm package can therefore update both manifests but refresh only the Cargo lockfile. The cascade, co-release floor and snapshot rewrite paths also need consistent manifest-local names after display promotion. These are contract failures, not exceptions to the native-resolution requirement; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
# Release execution

The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities.
- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. Several identities can currently derive operations addressing the same physical tag or forge release; shared ownership is not yet a separate authority.
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish.

## Layers

| Layer | Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |

## Two routes, one executor

```
local:  derive_unreleased_decision (untagged versions)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
```

- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

Local selection currently counts local tags as released. If tag creation succeeds but its push or GitHub work fails, a fresh bare `release` can exclude that package and report `Nothing to release.`. The executor can recover a retained intent; tag-filtered selection can discard it before execution. The committed-roster route avoids that selection shortcut. This remains a violation of the retry contract, tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Run envelope and state (`release.rs`)

- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.

## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)

- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup falls back to paging the release list (`provider/forge.rs`).

The intended tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package. Derivation currently gates by distribution identity, so one dual Cargo/npm owner's shared tag and public release can precede its other registry publish. This is a contract failure, not a fixed ecosystem order. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.

## Wire and observation boundaries

Stdout JSON reports include `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`; durable decision, intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files retain their own wire shapes. `release-pr verify` currently rejects decide's enveloped stdout when the action passes it unchanged. File-output inspection alone does not test that producer/consumer boundary.

Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. PyPI observation accepts a matching file rather than the intended wheel/sdist set, and any matching yanked file produces Absent. Artifact size/sha256 validation currently applies to declared GitHub assets, not a complete registry-output inventory. Required file-set recovery and separate private-index read/upload routes are planned, not shipped guarantees.

## Verification tiers

- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns.
- Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`.
- Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`.
# Package identity

How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Dual-manifest package: one directory with several admitted canonical manifests; one graph package, one version grammar and several distribution identities. Cargo+npm is supported by the model; co-located Cargo+Python currently fails with E007 because their grammars differ, including a Maturin dynamic Python version.
- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.

## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)

| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo:foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |

- `parse` treats text before the first `:` or `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare.
- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
- `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name.
- Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11).
- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
  - Different names never match.
  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
- A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership.

## Resolving ambiguity

A workspace can hold `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion. Canonical-only new references are planned in [the v1 design](polyglot-v1.md), not implemented by today's parser.

- `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. Some status helpers still use `PackageId::resolve_unique`, a scan over display ids; these are not equivalent for dual-manifest packages with different native names.
- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: two linear passes over the rules in declaration order, prefixed rules first, then bare. It never sorts the rules. A bare rule that reaches a promoted name is an `AmbiguousName` error, using `ResolvedConfig::promoted_siblings`.
- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.

## Loading a workspace

`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):

1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids, then names promoted into several ecosystems are recorded as `promoted_siblings`.
4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.

## Historical ownership

For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `sole_owner_at` checks which same-named candidate's first current canonical manifest path exists at the tag's commit; it does not read every historical manifest name. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies that ownership check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner.

This is not complete rename, manifest-addition or demotion support. Removing a sibling can stop lookup of a newer qualified tag, and current paths can misidentify historic bare ownership. Those failures remain tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md); do not infer migration safety from the directory key alone.

## Platform packages in code

| Step | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` |
| Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` |
| Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` |
| List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` |
| Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) |
| Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform |

- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.

# Codex Agent Roles

These are portable role instructions for Codex multi-agent work. They are resources, not a Codex TOML configuration surface: a skill reads the applicable card before it asks the host to delegate a bounded task.

The primary agent owns task decomposition, shared interfaces, final artifact assembly, verification, and all external writes. A role card defines a cognitive boundary, not a substitute owner.

| Role | Use for | Recommended tier |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `recon` | File, API, and evidence inventory | `gpt-5.6-luna` / low |
| `tracer` | Control-flow, data-flow, and boundary tracing | `gpt-5.6-terra` / medium |
| `research` | Bounded internal or external evidence collection | `gpt-5.6-terra` / medium |
| `author` | A defined draft with fixed inputs and output schema | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `implementer` | An isolated implementation batch with fixed interfaces | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `adversary` | Independent refutation or counterexample search | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `reviewer` | Evidence-led code or artifact review | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `judge` | Binding synthesis or exit decision | `gpt-5.6-sol` / high |

Use the recommended tier only when the host lets the primary agent choose it. If it does not, preserve the role boundary and run with the host default. If multi-agent work is unavailable, perform the same bounded passes sequentially in the primary agent.

## Delegation packet

Before requesting a teammate, provide this packet after reading the selected role card. The packet is the task boundary; the role card supplies the cognitive mode.

| Field | Required content |
| :--- | :--- |
| Role | One card from this directory and why that cognitive mode fits. |

name: plugin-management
description: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access.
---

# Plugin Management

Use the Plugin Management app to discover useful integrations and manage
existing plugins. Choose the most direct capability for the user's task before
searching for anything new.

## Choose the right capability

1. Use an available built-in tool when it already provides the needed
   capability. General web search, image generation, memory, and sites do not
   require a plugin unless the user requests a specific external provider or a
   capability unavailable natively.
2. Use an already connected plugin when it can complete the task.
3. Search for a plugin when an external app, account, service, or data source
   would materially improve the result and no available tool can access it.

Infer plugin intent from the user's actual task. Requests involving email,
calendars, messaging, documents, project management, customer systems, finance,
or analytics may need an external integration even when the user never says
"plugin," "install," or "connect."

Before saying an external service is unavailable, requesting pasted data, or
proposing a manual workaround, determine whether a relevant plugin exists.

## Find and suggest plugins

Call `search_plugins` with concise provider names, product names, or capability
keywords. For example, use `Gmail`, `calendar`, or `project management`, not
the entire user request. The currently available tools and any recommended
plugin list are not a complete directory.

When a relevant unconnected plugin would help, call `suggest_plugins` with its
exact returned plugin ID. Suggest the smallest useful set, preferably three or
fewer. Do not suggest plugins that are already installed or already pending.

Suggestions do not block the task. Continue any work that does not require the
connection and briefly explain what still needs the user's action. Never claim
a plugin is installed or connected without verification. Use its tools only
after its individual connection is confirmed.

## Manage existing plugins

- Use `get_app_permissions` to inspect a plugin's permissions.
- Use `update_app_permissions` only for a permission change the user requested.
  Ask before ambiguous, broad, or risky changes.
- Use `get_plugin_dependencies` to inspect required apps or dependencies.
- Use `uninstall_app` only when the user explicitly requests removal. Correct
  an obvious spelling mistake when the intended plugin is unambiguous, and pass
  its actual name without inventing an identifier.

Keep user-facing explanations focused on the task, connection state, and
requested change. Do not expose internal tool names or claim actions happened
without checking their results.

# Recon

Use for deterministic inventory, not conclusions. Enumerate files, entry points, manifests, schemas, symbols, tests, and existing artifacts within the assigned boundary.

Return exact paths, identifiers, commands run, and observations. Separate facts from unresolved questions. Do not edit files, recommend a design, or infer reachability from a name alone.
# Adversary

Use to independently try to falsify a draft, implementation claim, reachability claim, or verification result. Seek counterexamples, omitted states, boundary crossings, invalid assumptions, and missing negative tests.

Return only evidence-backed findings with exact locations and a concrete failing scenario when applicable. Do not rewrite the artifact, convert suspicion into a defect without evidence, or issue the final decision.

name: implement
description: Execute an approved plan or specification with targeted implementation, tests, evidence, review, and independent verification. Use for “implement this”, “execute the plan”, “build this feature”, “write the code”, or “refactor without changing behavior”.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Implement with evidence

## Outcome

Make the requested workspace change in bounded batches and return a scoped verdict grounded in current code, risk-based verification, and defect-family review.

## Workflow

1. Prefer a persisted `plan@1`. Read it from `plan_file_path` and its source spec from `spec_file_path`; validate them with `shared/schemas/plan@1.json` and `shared/schemas/spec@1.json`.
2. Verify the plan’s `spec_hash` against the raw spec file bytes. Stop and report drift if it differs; a stale plan cannot silently govern implementation.
3. Produce `workspace-manifest@1` from current repository state, every affected language, project-native verification capabilities, baseline tests, and exposed workflow provenance.
4. Execute one cohesive subsystem batch. Choose the smallest safe implementation and verification methods from the changed risks and `shared/references/verification/evidence.md`.
5. Record `implementation-result@1` with exact criterion locations, commands, observations, boundaries, and environment evidence.
6. Use available mutation tooling against changed behavior or a safe deliberate-fault check. Record `mutation-report@2`; unavailable evidence is a coverage gap.
7. Produce `implementation-review@2`. Judge verification fit, sibling completeness, semantic models, and architecture.
8. Before completion, account for every planned batch and started verification task, reread persisted artifacts and current code, independently challenge semantic completeness, and emit scoped `verdict@3`. Commit only after user authorization.

## Defect-family review

Before reviewing, load `shared/references/verification/implementation-review.md` and the evidence it selects. For each changed defect, assess:

- Syntactic siblings with the same code shape or algorithm.
- Semantic siblings with the same domain responsibility or failure state.
- Candidate sites supporting semantic completeness, including zero-match claims.
- The shared root cause for related instances.
- Missing concepts, states, operations, boundaries, abstractions, invariants, or enforcement.
- One disposition: fix instances, unify implementation, escalate architecture, or explicitly defer.
- Boundary reach, input-space method, relevant environments, external-state freshness, and coverage gaps.

Use the current architecture model when available to derive candidate responsibilities and canonical abstractions. Resolve `changes_requested` findings before the exit gate. Route `needs_architecture` to `scribe:architect`; gate the resulting spec, amend the plan, then resume.

## Contract

- Input schemas: `shared/schemas/plan@1.json` and `shared/schemas/spec@1.json`
- Workspace schema: `shared/schemas/workspace-manifest@1.json`
- Batch schema: `shared/schemas/implementation-result@1.json`
- Mutation schema: `shared/schemas/mutation-report@2.json`
- Review schema: `shared/schemas/implementation-review@2.json`
- Output schema: `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`
- Durable inputs: `docs/projects/<linked_spec>.json` and `docs/specs/<id>.json` when their path fields are set
- Evidence: per-task `criteria_evidence` points to current implementation and tests; it is not a substitute for final inspection.

## Teams and fallback

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`; use `implementer` only for an isolated batch and `reviewer` only after its diff and verification output exist.

Use teams only for independent subsystem batches with no shared files or undecided interfaces. Give each teammate a batch, criteria, current manifest, and persisted paths. Reconcile changed files and observed outputs; track every started task to a terminal result. Work alone for coupled boundaries or when teams are unavailable.

## Exceptions and recovery

- If the implementation contradicts a spec criterion, halt remaining work and report `spec_contradiction` with the criterion ID, spec claim, observed behavior, and evidence. Route the correction to `scribe:correct-spec`, then replan in amend mode.
- If the safe solution needs an architectural boundary beyond plan scope, stop that batch and report an architecture escalation grounded in live code. Do not commit an unsafe shape just to complete the plan.
- If related defects reveal a missing domain concept, state, operation, boundary, abstraction, invariant, or enforcement mechanism, route `implementation-review@2` to `scribe:architect` before continuing.
- If one batch cannot be implemented safely within plan scope, route its `implementation-result@1` architecture escalation to `scribe:architect`.
- If a test or build fails, diagnose from the observed output and fix only the relevant defect before continuing. Do not mask a failure by weakening verification.

## Boundaries

- Do not make external releases, push branches, or commit without user authorization.
- Do not claim success from a passing targeted test when the applicable full suite has not been considered.
- Do not accept teammate summaries without reading the changed files, test output, and evidence yourself.
- Do not require mutation, property, fuzz, boundary, or environment checks when the changed risk does not justify them.
- Do not claim support from a named tool alone; record what it exercised and observed.

name: gate
description: Independently verify an artifact against its criteria before it crosses a lifecycle boundary. Use for requirements, specs, plans, implementations, PRs, and explicit readiness checks.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Gate a lifecycle artifact with evidence

Sentinel judges an existing artifact; it does not author a replacement. Begin by identifying what the artifact claims, where it is persisted, and which criteria actually govern it.

## Workflow

1. Identify `artifact_type`, `artifact_path`, the authoritative criteria, linked artifacts, and source files that can prove or disprove each criterion.
2. Read persisted files when a path is present rather than relying on conversation summaries.
3. Build an evidence table that classifies each criterion as verified, failed, or unverifiable, with exact paths and test or inspection evidence.
4. Produce `verdict@3` conforming to `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`. Name the verified scope, blockers, coverage gaps, and pending checks.
5. Pass only when every applicable criterion is verified. On failure, return specific blockers that the producing workflow can act on.

## Retry protocol

On a retry, inspect only the revised artifact and the previous blockers. Do not reopen unrelated review scope. Set `retry_count` accurately and escalate to the caller after the third failed retry rather than looping indefinitely.

## Evidence and safety

- Do not treat a passing test alone as proof of a criterion it does not exercise.
- Mark evidence unverifiable when the relevant source, environment, or criterion is absent; do not convert uncertainty into a pass.
- Treat a required check that has not finished as pending and fail the gate.
- Do not edit the artifact, create a PR, or publish a verdict externally unless the user asks for a separate action.

## Team use

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`; use `recon` for fixed evidence collection, but reserve the binding decision for the primary `judge`.

When teams are available, split criterion verification only across independent subsystems after the artifact and criteria are fixed. The owner reconciles coverage and delivers one binding verdict. Without teams, verify each criterion sequentially with the same standard.

name: pr
description: Draft or open a reviewer-ready pull request from verified work. Use when the user asks to create a PR or write its description; require confirmation before any remote action.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Open a reviewable pull request

Ground the PR in the actual branch diff, target branch, linked lifecycle artifacts, and executed verification. A reviewer should be able to understand the intent, evidence, and residual risk without reconstructing the branch history.

## Evidence to collect

- Compare the current branch to its intended base and inspect the full diff.
- Read linked `shared/schemas/requirement@1.json`, `shared/schemas/spec@1.json`, or persisted artifact paths only when they apply to the change.
- Record verification commands and their observed outcomes. Do not claim checks that were not run.
- Identify migrations, operational follow-up, known limitations, and intentionally deferred work.

## Draft shape

Write a concise title and body with:

- An outcome-led summary of user-visible or architectural intent.
- Observed verification with exact commands or inspections and results.
- Reasons and coverage gaps for checks not run.
- Risks, migrations, limitations, or follow-up only when they apply.
- Existing issue, requirement, spec, plan, or changeset links only when they help review.

Use enough summary bullets to explain one coherent change. If the summary reveals independent topics, recommend separate PRs or state the dependency that requires one delivery.

Show the exact title, body, labels, base branch, and repository target before creating anything remotely. Create the PR only after explicit user confirmation.

## Team use

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`; use `recon` for linked-criteria inventory or `reviewer` for verification-output review, never for the final PR narrative.

When agent teams are available, use parallel work only for independent evidence collection: one teammate may inventory linked criteria while another summarizes verification output. Reconcile both against the live diff yourself. If teams are unavailable, collect those inputs sequentially and produce the same result.

## Safety

- Do not publish a draft as a PR, assign reviewers, add labels, or alter the target branch without user confirmation.
- Do not fabricate issue links, test results, or acceptance evidence.

CLI-OUT-05: With `--format json`, the status, add, init, pre and snapshot reports on stdout are single JSON objects with camelCase keys and a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` (the subcommand name) and `dryRun`.
CLI-ADD-01: `callisto add --package <name>:<severity> --summary <text>` (--package repeatable, bare or qualified names such as `cargo/app`, severity none, patch, minor or major) writes `.changeset/<adjective>-<noun>-<verb>.md` with front matter mapping each package to its severity and the trimmed summary as body, prints `Added changeset: <path>`, and never prompts.
CLI-INIT-01: Before any question, `callisto init` prints `Detected:` with the ecosystems, the origin remote URL, and each package's qualified id, version, last tag, and binary names for binary-producing packages.
CLI-INIT-02: Interactive init asks only: versioning (independent or fixed); whether to ship binaries as GitHub release assets, only when a package produces a binary; the product package, only when more than one does; the forge repository, pre-filled from origin; comma-separated target triples; whether to generate a workflow (default no); and whether to write callisto.toml (default yes).
CLI-INIT-12: init exits 1 without writing for an empty or repeated target triple, --artifact-target when no package produces a binary, a --product-package that is absent or not binary-producing, a --forge-repository that is not `owner/repo` or differs from origin's GitHub repository, or --forge-repository or --product-package given without --artifact-target.
CLI-WF-03: Without artifact slots or platform packages, the generated workflow triggers on push to the detected default branch (local `origin/HEAD`, else a live query of `origin`, else the checked-out branch, else `main`) and has two jobs: `version-pr` running callisto-action with `mode: version-pr` and that same `branch`, and `release` running it with `mode: release` and a token secret per detected ecosystem (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN with NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE, PYPI_TOKEN) plus GH_TOKEN. init's human-readable output names which of those sources resolved the branch.
CLI-WF-04: When binaries ship as artifact slots or the workspace has napi platform packages, the generated workflow has `version-pr`, `plan` (runs `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` when the pushed commit adds or modifies .callisto/release-decision.json), `build` (a matrix from napi targets and artifact slots), and `execute` (runs `callisto release artifact-manifest` and `callisto release execute`) jobs.
CLI-WF-06: For a workspace with maturin platform targets, or platform packages without napi targets, init prints `Skipping GitHub Actions workflow generation: <reason>.`, records a warning diagnostic in the JSON report, and exits 1 instead when --workflow was given.
CLI-SCHEMA-01: `callisto schema` prints the StatusReport JSON Schema; `--type` is a fixed value enum selecting another report type, and an unrecognized value is a clap usage error (exit 2) listing the supported values.
REL-CMD-01: `callisto release` selects every package that has a publish target other than `none` and whose current version has no matching tag. For each one it runs the registry publishes, creates the git tag, and creates the GitHub release when `github-release` is a target.
REL-CMD-08: A malformed `--package` value fails with `E227` and an unknown package with E102. A duplicate selection, an already-tagged version, or a package with no publish target fails with E169.
REL-CMD-12: `--format json` output of `release`, `release --dry-run`, `release plan`, `release execute` and `release artifact-manifest` goes through the same envelope every other command's JSON report uses: a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` (the subcommand name) and `dryRun`, alongside that subcommand's own payload fields unchanged. The intent and artifact-manifest --out files, receipt --receipt file and version --emit-decision file use their durable document shape without command or dryRun wrapper fields.
REL-AUTH-01: `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path>` takes the package and version roster from the decision file committed in that commit. It does not re-run changeset, group, cascade or pre-release selection.
REL-AUTH-02: `release plan --from-release-commit` fails with E165 and writes no output file in any of these cases: HEAD is not the given commit; the commit neither adds nor modifies the decision file; it deletes no changeset `.md` file; a claimed package's manifest does not change to its claimed version; a claimed package's changelog is unchanged; an unclaimed manifest version changes; or a claimed package is not found.
REL-AUTH-03: A committed decision file whose digest does not match its entries fails with E166. Decision schema versions 1 and 2 are accepted, and any other version fails with an error naming the version found.
REL-ORD-01: A graph package's tag is created only after all selected registry publishes belonging to its canonical manifests succeed, and its GitHub release draft only after its tag. A `[[release.artifact]]` slot's upload follows the product's draft and gates the product's publish even when a different selected package owns the asset, and the release is published only after the draft and every upload.
REL-ORD-02: A selected package publishes after the selected packages it depends on through runtime, build, optional or dev edges. A dev edge between two packages in the same dependency cycle does not order them, and a runtime, build or optional cycle fails with E104.
REL-PUB-04: PyPI publish runs `python3 -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist/` in the package directory, falling back to `python` and failing with E170 when neither is on PATH. It then runs `twine upload dist/<normalized-name>-<version>*` with `--repository-url` for a configured index, adding `--skip-existing` only for the default index, `upload.pypi.org` or `test.pypi.org`.
REL-PUB-08: PyPI observation fetches `<index>/<normalized-name>/` (default `https://pypi.org/simple`) with `curl` and `Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json`. In a 200 JSON body, any matching yanked file means absent; otherwise at least one matching non-yanked file means present, without checking an expected wheel/sdist set. A 404 or no matching file means absent, and a non-JSON body or other non-retryable status is indeterminate. Transient HTTP statuses use the observation retry policy.
REL-RERUN-01: An operation whose result is already present and identical is recorded as already satisfied, and its effect is not repeated. For a registry version, stderr shows `warning: <package> <version> is already published; skipping`.
REL-RERUN-02: After a run fails partway, rerunning the same command with no state file from the failed run performs only the missing operations and writes a receipt. A local annotated tag on the expected commit that is missing on the remote is pushed before the receipt is written, regardless of its annotation text.
REL-RERUN-04: A receipt is written only when every operation ends `published` or `alreadySatisfied`, and otherwise the run exits 1 with no receipt file (E172 when operations remain incomplete). The receipt records `intentDigest`, the envelope (`orchestrationRevision`, `releaseSourceRevision`, intent and artifact-manifest digests), and each operation's outcome and provider evidence.
REL-GH-07: In the release workflow, `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` reaches only the `execute` job's execute step. The workflow's default permissions are empty, and the plan and build jobs receive no registry credential.
REL-PR-02: `release-pr decide` fails in these cases: an invalid repository (E141), an unsafe branch name (E142), duplicate PR numbers (E143), a snapshot for another repository or base branch (E144), a managed-branch PR from a fork (E145), more than one managed PR (E146), a malformed SHA suffix (E147), or a PR headed at `<release-branch>--staging` (E154). Each of these carries its own code even when `--snapshot`/`--decision` is a file, inline JSON, or stdin. `release-pr verify` exits 0 when a fresh snapshot equals the decision's snapshot and fails with E148 otherwise.
REL-PR-04: The release-PR action runs the version command with `--emit-decision <decision_path>` (default `.callisto/release-decision.json`). It commits the result with GitHub's `createCommitOnBranch` on `<release-branch>--staging` reset to the base commit, and refuses unless the remote tree equals the locally staged tree. It then moves the release branch ref through the REST API and never runs `git push`. Before creating the commit, before moving the ref, and before any label or PR write, it runs `callisto release-pr verify` against a fresh snapshot and stops when verification fails.
REL-PR-06: `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto` default `version` input `latest` installs the callisto release the action's own invocation is pinned to (`github.action_ref` resolved against `orin-dx/callisto`'s `callisto@` tags), falling back to the newest published release only when that ref is unset or matches no tag. An explicit `version` input overrides this resolution.
REL-PR-07: `--format json` output of `release-pr verify`, `release-pr decide` and `release-pr commit-plan` (without `--out`) goes through the same envelope every other command's JSON report uses: a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`, alongside that subcommand's own payload fields unchanged.
VER-AGG-02: An entry name resolves to a workspace package by prefixed id (`cargo/foo`) or bare name; a bare name that matches packages in two or more ecosystems aborts the run with an ambiguous-name error (E103).
VER-CAS-05: Coverage: an exact spec covers only the equal version, a bare Cargo version is a caret requirement, a caret requirement never covers a prerelease, a Cargo `workspace = true` spec is tested using the root `[workspace.dependencies]` spec, and an npm `workspace:` spec always covers. A catalog or other untestable spec is treated as covering and never rewritten; a catalog spec emits a CatalogSpecNotRewritten warning.
VER-CAS-06: A spec that no longer covers the new version is rewritten to it, keeping the operator and precision for Cargo and npm (`^1.2` becomes `^2.0` for 2.0.0), or to the exact version for npm when `preserve-npm-ranges = false`. A runtime, optional, build or peer dependent that is itself released in this run, for any reason, has every such spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the dependency's new version the same way, even when the spec still covers it; a dependent that is not releasing keeps its spec unless out of range. `workspace = true`, npm `workspace:` and catalog specs are never rewritten by either rule, and a dev dependent's spec is rewritten only when out of range. A spec that cannot be rewritten mechanically, such as an npm range with spaces, `||`, a hyphen or a wildcard, is left unchanged with a RangeNotRoundTrippable warning.
VER-CAS-07: A rewrite names the dependency as the dependent's own ecosystem spells it, so an npm dependent of a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names is rewritten under the npm name. A Cargo dependency inherited with `workspace = true` is rewritten in the workspace root's `[workspace.dependencies]`, not in the member manifest.
VER-PRE-01: `callisto pre enter <tag>` writes `.changeset/pre.json` with `mode` `pre`, the tag, every package's current version under `initialVersions`, keyed by its display id (`foo`, or `cargo/foo` when another ecosystem has a `foo`) and an empty `changesets` list, then stages the file with git; under `--dry-run` it prints the content and writes nothing. For promoted packages, an older bare key is assigned to the unique historical owner at the commit that added pre.json; if no unique owner exists, version fails with E245.
VER-PRE-03: In pre mode, a bumped package's version is its `initialVersions` entry bumped by its severity plus `-{tag}.N`, where N starts at 0 and increments while the release part is unchanged (0.1.0 with a minor changeset and tag `beta` gives 0.2.0-beta.0, then 0.2.0-beta.1); PEP 440 packages use `aN` for tags `a`/`alpha`, `bN` for `b`/`beta`, `rcN` for `rc`/`c`/`pre`/`preview` (case-insensitive), and `.devN` for any other tag.
VER-PRE-08: A snapshot writes manifests and refreshes each active ecosystem's existing lockfile, unconditionally (there is no `--no-refresh-lockfiles` for `snapshot`), so a subsequent locked install resolves against the snapshot version; it ignores and keeps pending changesets, writes no changelog or `pre.json`, and stages nothing in git; under `--dry-run` it writes nothing.
VER-PRE-09: For every workspace dependency whose current spec does not cover the snapshot version, `snapshot` rewrites that spec in the dependent's own manifest, using the dependent's ecosystem and the dependency's name as registered for that ecosystem; a spec that already covers the snapshot version is left unchanged.
VER-APPLY-01: `version` writes the new version to every canonical manifest of a bumped package, so both manifests of a dual-manifest package move together.
VER-APPLY-08: Outside pre mode, a successful `version` deletes the consumed changeset files, then stages every written manifest and changelog, `pre.json` changes, the existing lockfiles of affected ecosystems, and the changeset deletions (via `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch`, which also succeeds for an already-deleted file).
VER-APPLY-10: `version --emit-decision <path>` writes the release decision JSON to `<path>` relative to the workspace root after the plan has been applied successfully: `schemaVersion` 2, a digest, and one entry per canonical manifest of each bumped package (ecosystem-qualified name, target version, reasons) sorted by package. Reason `kind` is `changeset`, `inference`, `fixedGroup` or `linkedGroup` (with `groupId`), `cascade` (with source package and edge kind, `peer` for peer escalation) or `preReleasePolicy` (with the prerelease tag).
VER-APPLY-13: After planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk version differs from its version at `HEAD` and either: the workspace's changesets directory still has a pending changeset as of `HEAD` (not yet consumed by a commit); or, outside an active pre-release cycle (`.changeset/pre.json` absent), a canonical manifest is staged in the git index but not yet committed. Both are the signature of a `version` run that wrote and staged its changes but never committed -- the second covers a changeset that was only ever a working-tree file (added and consumed by `version` without ever being committed), which the first check cannot see. A repository with no commits yet, a manifest/changesets directory that didn't exist at `HEAD`, or an active pre-release cycle (which legitimately reruns `version` without a commit in between) is never refused this way.
VER-APPLY-14: By default, applying a plan refreshes each active ecosystem's lockfile that exists on disk: `cargo update --workspace` for Cargo; for Pypi, `uv lock` if `uv.lock` exists, else `poetry lock --no-update` if `poetry.lock` exists, else `pdm lock --update-reuse` if `pdm.lock` exists; for Npm, `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` for `package-lock.json`, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn install --mode update-lockfile` for `yarn.lock`, and `bun install --lockfile-only` for `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb`, each independently when its lockfile is present. `--no-refresh-lockfiles` skips this; `--refresh-lockfiles` is accepted but has no effect.
VER-APPLY-15: A lockfile refresh command that exits non-zero aborts `version` with E208 naming the lockfile and the exact command that failed, instead of recording the failure and continuing.

content.text: The repo has one important stacking constraint: PR CI currently runs only for PRs targeting `main`. I’ll use main-targeted cumulative stacks with parent-only review diffs, then rebase children as parents merge. That preserves CI without changing workflow policy. Independent lanes can run in separate worktrees, but agents won’t share writable files or run Cargo builds concurrently.

# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. Evidence and implementation work are recorded in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Proposed decision

- Use canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution references for new authored and generated data; native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Read legacy references through a deliberate compatibility/migration boundary. Preserve historical tag ownership without using display promotion as a release-identity change.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

The exact owner representation, legacy colon-form handling, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve those unspecified details or introduce release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- [System findings and verification limits](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

# V1 implementation and stacked-PR execution

Status: execution portfolio for owner review. Baseline: main `8ef9aa5a4` (#168), plus the uncommitted documentation reconciliation. This document plans changes; it does not authorize implementation, commits, worktrees, pushes, remote PR creation or publication. [Task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

## Start with three independent lanes

First preserve and review the documentation changes as a foundation PR. Do not mix their current-behavior corrections into the urgent release bug fix or discard them while creating worktrees. If the release fix must land first, its worktree starts from main and carries only the relevant spec/docs changes; reconcile the foundation afterward.

| Lane | PR-sized units | Dependency or constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release/wire | T01 producer/consumer fix → T02 schema repair → T03 contextual decisions → T03-PRE baselines; T03-HISTORY inherited/root verification follows T03 | One writer for `release.rs`/`version.rs`; T03-HISTORY and T03-PRE both touch shared graph consumers and integrate serially |
| Native resolution | T04 manifest-local names → T04-PNPM protocols → T04-LOCK refresh | Independent of the release-PR fix; reserve dependency/resolver/cascade/apply files for this lane |
| Installer | T11 version/source fidelity | Shell-only lane; independent of model changes and safe to delegate narrowly |
| Early workflows | T10-BINS binary inventory/unsupported builders → T10-AUTH native auth | Start after T03-HISTORY releases `cargo.rs`; one writer for generated `init.rs` and action execution scripts |
| Apply recovery join | T05 input retention and partial-run detection | Needs T03-HISTORY + T04-LOCK; fault injection is part of this PR, not deferred to the final matrix |

T01 is the v0.9 release-path priority. Its merge permits the bot to regenerate the release PR; fresh decision/source agreement and passing CI must precede any separately authorized merge/publication. Other lanes do not automatically become v0.9 release requirements. Existing-contract fixes can run while the architectural decisions below are being reviewed.

## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects/retry | T08 shared physical effects → T08-RETRY tagged-candidate completion | One owner per irreversible effect; required publications gate announcements; local retry does not lose push/forge work |
| Python completion | T09 required file-set recovery → T09-ROUTES read/upload destinations | Complete declared files, not first-file presence; no changed bytes or untrusted destination on retry |
| Workflow integration | T10 intent-selected outputs → T10-NAPI lifecycle ownership | No unrelated builds or duplicate publication authority; native preparation/packing still works |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY and T07 are sibling branches on T06, but share identity/version consumers: one integration owner must reserve their overlapping files and serialize overlapping edits. T08 waits for both. After T08, T08-RETRY and T09 may run in parallel only with disjoint write reservations; shared model/executor/simulator changes are authored in the parent first. T09-ROUTES follows T09 because both own the registry adapter. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: decisions needed before model implementation

The owner has approved scope and direction, not every wire shape or compatibility rule. Recommendations below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | Always emit slash-qualified native IDs; retain qualified colon input as a compatibility spelling; read old bare records only through unique owned migration | Decide whether new interactive/bare CLI input is rejected or accepted with an explicit migration warning; fixtures for config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | Current Cargo/npm/PyPI required publications before shared tag and public GitHub release; retain draft-after-tag unless a supported fixture requires otherwise | Confirm exact owner completion boundary and duplicate-effect diagnostics; future Go tag is publication, not a completion-only marker |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| NAPI hooks | Callisto owns publication/tag/forge effects; native tooling owns build/pack preparation | Specify supported hook configuration/migration without blanket suppression of legitimate user hooks; prove a hook cannot independently publish siblings or announce |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from the dirty shared checkout.
- Current CI triggers only for PRs targeting `main` in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`. Default: open cumulative child branches against `main`, label the dependency in the description, and include the parent-only review range. Retargeting to a parent branch would skip this CI; do not do that without a separately approved CI-trigger change.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Rebase/restack the child onto updated main and rerun applicable checks before merging it. Inspect actual commit topology after squash/rebase merges; do not assume GitHub removes parent commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.
- Commit/PR actions remain coordinator-owned and owner-approved. Workers never push, merge, approve CI, edit release policy or publish versions.

## Plugin execution route

Use a light route for existing defects and the fuller route only when a domain contract changes. Do not make every small shell patch run the complete requirement lifecycle.

| Situation | Plugins/skills | Artifact or check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Already verified current-contract defect | Navigator packet → Smith bounded implementation → Ranger targeted sibling/defect-family review → Sentinel scoped verification | Exact diff, regression/fault evidence, current criterion mapping and remaining checks |
| Canonical ownership, native authority or output-proof change | Scribe architecture/spec work and applicable audit/verify/gate steps → Navigator amendment → Smith → independent review/Sentinel | Owner-confirmed contract, versioned wire policy, interface inventory and raw spec hash |
| New domain gap discovered during implementation | Stop only that batch; Scribe architect/spec correction and Navigator amendment | Evidence-backed escalation; do not silently invent a second semantic model |
| New request beyond this scope | Weaver capture/connect/clarify only as needed | Traceable need; no unapproved requirement becomes a gate |
| User-visible release impact | Courier changeset | Verified topic-specific entry targeting `callisto-cli` |
| Commit and stacked PR handoff | Courier commit/PR after permission | Parent-only diff, full-stack evidence, base branch, migration risks and authorized remote action |

Plugins guide reasoning and evidence; they do not themselves provide isolated worktrees, a branch scheduler or authorization. Final synthesis, interface decisions and binding readiness stay with the coordinator. Sentinel must report pending/unverifiable evidence rather than converting a targeted test into a whole-release pass.

## Agent and model allocation

Prefer the host's inherited model unless a bounded job benefits from a deliberate smaller override. The currently exposed delegation runtime permits `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and the parent frontier model; do not rely on unavailable role-card model names or promise costs/latencies.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Paths, symbols, test commands and branch/CI inventory | `gpt-6-luna`, low effort, recon | Read-only deterministic inventory; no architectural verdict |
| Shell installer fixtures, link/schema checks, fixed doc edits | Small model at low/medium effort where the interface is fixed | Explicit files and expected cases; escalate failed reasoning instead of lowering verification |
| Straightforward parser/lock/auth correction | Workhorse model, medium effort; raise effort for alias/auth subtleties | One subsystem, fixed owner contract and native regression |
| Canonical identity, historical authority, DAG/proofs and partial-upload semantics | Coordinator/strong model, high effort | Own cross-crate interfaces and failure semantics; no concurrent competing models |
| Implementation once interfaces are fixed | Workhorse implementer, medium/high effort | One isolated task/worktree with no shared write set |
| Independent challenge/review | Separate workhorse reviewer, high effort for model/retry changes | Read final diff plus tests; never rely on the author's self-certification |

Start with two implementing workers plus one read-only reviewer/recon, not an agent per finding. Increase concurrency only when there are disjoint, unblocked tasks and the coordinator can inspect every result. A packet contains objective, persisted paths/hashes, owned files, exclusions, criterion/test cases, dependencies and a completion condition. Workers preserve other changes and return changed paths, commands, actual outcomes, skips and unresolved concerns.

No concurrent Cargo builds/tests locally, even across tasks. Reserve one build slot; use sequential scoped runs and reuse the shared cache. Read-only analysis, shell-only tests, review and drafting can run while that slot is occupied. Worktree/build-directory changes need approval where they change environment or resource use; they are not a reason to bypass the repository's build rule.

2. Run the scoped commands in the task JSON sequentially; use native pack/install/build evidence where semantics require it. Test negative, stale, partial and conflicting states, not only a successful fresh release.

- Status changeset attribution and well-formedness checks still scan display ids through `PackageId::resolve_unique`, while version aggregation uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`. Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
- NAPI publication hooks can own the same platform/GitHub effects as Callisto. Official hook behavior and Callisto's lifecycle-enabled npm argv establish the risk; a combined generated-workflow fixture is still required (T10).
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes, complete Python files or the desired npm dist-tag. Artifact-set completion is a correctness fix (T09); universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- PyPI yanking is per file. The current classifier treats any matching yanked file as Absent even alongside non-yanked files. A yank is not deletion or permission to overwrite; confirm conflict/partial semantics with the required-output model (T09).
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. - No measured evidence establishes the owner's first-published-release-in-under-ten-minutes goal. Run fresh repositories with the documented steps and native credentials (T12).

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

## v0.9 handoff

Prioritize T01 to unblock release-PR refresh. Then require fresh release-source/decision agreement and passing workflow checks before merging the refreshed PR; do not merge the stale #113 decision as a workaround. The recorded E281 failure explains why the bot could not refresh it after later merges. No claim that E281 is the only possible publication blocker is established until the actual self-release succeeds.

The publication intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files are written without the stdout report envelope, so the same wrapper mismatch was not found there. That source inspection does not replace executing the publish path.
